presentation.title_rationale: The previous headline ran 91 characters, buried the topic behind a methodology frame ('a capability envelope you can audit') and carried a year label. The selected title front-loads production debugging agents, then answers the question an on-call reader actually holds during an outage: read-only is four controls, and the agent's tool policy is not one of the enforced three. The premise is carried by the PostgreSQL, CDP and fixture evidence already in the body, and the title promises no measured speed or safety number. At 62 characters it fits without truncation, so no long_title_reason is needed.
presentation.visual_purpose: A four-row schematic showing which layer refuses a write — the agent's tool policy (dashed, labelled 'the agent's own promise') versus credential scope, database read-only transaction and runtime expression guard — plus the recorded local fixture totals (9 scripted calls, 4 allowed, 5 refused, 4 rules, SQLite 3.45.1, CPython 3.12.3, no model invoked). It explains the article's central distinction visually; it is not a vendor diagram and shows no product UI.
